Timing: 14:00–16:00

The Ghana result is not exact age, flow-path or reaction validation. It is an operational evidence-ceiling diagnosis under a predeclared gate, with a synthetic check supporting the direction of the result. Removing strontium and silica moved about 52 percent of wells to non-identifiable, while fit metrics and bootstrap stability remained high. This shows why conventional good-fit criteria can conceal loss of mechanistic resolution.

Timing: 16:00–17:50

In the independent generator, chemistry added strong topology-ranking information and its PR-AUC gain survived family-wise correction. The +0.0091 hydraulic PR-AUC contrast did not survive correction, although Brier and log-loss improvements did. The −0.0060 age ranking contrast also did not survive correction and supplies no evidence of positive value. The conclusion is conditional complementarity, not that every stream always helps.

Timing: 21:30–22:45

The development stage selected a local-first/global-fallback estimator and it was tested once on 128 fresh locked cases. The PR-AUC point estimate was higher, but its family-wise simultaneous interval crossed zero; Brier score and log loss also failed the all-outcome superiority gate. Leave-one-edge-out robust global weighting worsened calibration. Therefore retain an estimator diagnostic, not a general superiority claim.
